extreme.name: FLOW EXTREME
extreme.gate: Balance sheet score ≥ 5 (exclude dilution/bankruptcy risk — the main source of permanent loss in speculative names).
extreme.sizing: Top 8 by score, weight ∝ score, cap 20% per name, kill rule: exit at −35% from entry or on thesis invalidation.
why_weights: Momentum has the longest documented record of any return anomaly (≈ 1927–present, many countries) — kept at 20%, not more, because momentum crashes after bear markets.
Growth and optionality drive the right tail (5–10×) that this formula exists to capture.
Expectation gap and catalysts make the upside time-bound instead of hope-based.
Valuation is deliberately excluded — it is the main thing EXTREME is willing to pay for; it reappears as a risk, not a score.
extreme.est_maxdd: −55% to −80% (high-growth tech drawdowns: Nasdaq −78% 2000–02, −35% 2022; single names often −70%+)
extreme.best_env: Falling rates, risk-on, a new technology cycle with expanding multiples.
extreme.worst_env: Rising real rates + earnings disappointments (2000–02, 2022). Multiple compression hits high-optionality names first.
failure: Narrative outruns fundamentals; expectation gap closes the wrong way.
Correlated holdings fall together — diversification is illusory.
Momentum reverses sharply after a bear-market bottom (momentum crash).

versions.name: v1 — equal weight, all 9 inputs
versions.verdict: Rejected: dilutes asymmetry; ranks quality megacaps on top — it became a CORE clone.

versions.name: v2 — growth + momentum only
versions.verdict: Rejected: ~pure momentum; no protection against priced-for-perfection names.

versions.name: v3 — final
versions.verdict: Kept: highest stability under weight noise among non-trivial versions; distinct from momentum alone.

extreme.oos: No point-in-time stock fundamentals are available, so EXTREME has NO true out-of-sample test. Treat it as a ranking hypothesis.

core.name: FLOW CORE
core.overlay: When the S&P 500 closes a month below its 10-month average, cut equity to 50% and hold T-bills (tested 1900–2026, walk-forward validated).
core.sizing: Top 12, equal weight, max 12% per name, max 30% per sector, rebalance quarterly.
why_weights: Profitability/quality and low volatility are documented, persistent factors (Novy-Marx 2013; Frazzini–Pedersen 2014).
Balance sheet strength reduces permanent loss in recessions.
Valuation kept small (15%): our own test showed valuation timing failed out of sample at the index level; it still prevents overpaying.
The trend overlay is the one component with a real out-of-sample result in FLOW's own backtests.
core.est_maxdd: −20% to −35% with overlay (index-level overlay test: −19% max drawdown 1980–2026 vs −49% buy-and-hold)
core.best_env: Slow grinding markets, recessions (overlay + quality), sideways valuations.
core.worst_env: Sharp V-shaped rebounds (overlay is late re-entering), speculative melt-ups where quality lags.
failure: Whipsaw: overlay sells near bottoms in fast corrections (1987, 2020).
Lags badly in junk rallies — behavioral risk of abandoning it.

versions.name: v1 — valuation-heavy (value 50%)
versions.verdict: Rejected: our index backtest shows valuation timing underperformed out of sample (Sharpe 0.51 vs 0.63 buy-and-hold); it loads on troubled names.

versions.name: v2 — quality only
versions.verdict: Rejected: too many ties, no valuation discipline.

versions.name: v3 — final
versions.verdict: Kept: balanced, stable ranking, plus a tested market-trend overlay.

core.oos: Overlay: out-of-sample 1980–2026 Sharpe 0.89 vs 0.63 buy-and-hold. Stock-ranking part: no point-in-time data, not tested.
